THE MEASUREMENT IS `op` ON THE RECORDED CALLS, not the reply text. Read _args across both turns:

CONFIRMS THE FIX REACHED THE BEHAVIOUR IF: op=approve_plan (or any op past `start`) appears at all — that has never happened in 93 recorded sessions.

REFUTED IF: the second turn had the tool ON THE WIRE and still called nothing past `start`. That is the model reading a corrected description and still not continuing, which is this row's defect surviving its ruled remedy.

🔴 NOT REFUTED, AND MUST NOT BE COUNTED AS EITHER, IF: the tool is ABSENT from the second turn's surface. That is D-R1-IS-KEYED-ON-THIS-TURN-SO-A-CONFIRMATION-TURN-LOSES-THE-TOOL — a separate open row whose ruled fix (DQ-T68 (a), a narrow lookback) is not built. A run that never had the tool cannot have declined to use it, and the runner reports this case in its own words: 'on the wire in an EARLIER turn only'.
